Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

the others pronoun

also all the others, the other ones, the rest of them, others

classical

Plin. Ep. 9.33.4: audentior cēterīs
Sen. Ep. 15.10: quid tibi cum cēterīs?

cēterī, cēterae, cētera

adjective, mostly plural; no masculine nominative singular

the others, all the rest

Lewis & Short: cēterī are the others besides those named, of the same kind; reliquī, those left over (see the rest).

Other words

  • reliquī, reliquae, reliqua — the others that remain, the remaining

    adjective (reliquus, reliqua, reliquum) · also used · classical · Varr. RR 2 praef. 1: reliquīs septem

    Those left when some have been taken out: reliquīs septem (diēbus), on the other seven days.

  • aliī, aliae, alia — others (not necessarily all the rest)

    plural of alius · also used · classical · Gell. 19.5.10: aliī indūtiās cum eā variē factitābant

    Others, some others; for “some … others”, see some.

Examples

  • hōc certāmine puer quīdam audentior cēterīs in ulteriōra tendēbat

    in this contest one boy, bolder than the others, kept swimming further outPlin. Ep. 9.33.4

  • quid tibi cum cēterīs? tē ipse antecessistī

    what are the others to you? you have outrun yourselfSen. Ep. 15.10

  • nec sibi sōlī, sed conjugī, līberīs cēterīsque, quōs cārōs habeat tuērīque dēbeat

    not for himself alone, but for his wife, his children and the others whom he holds dear and ought to protectCic. Off. 1.12

  • sacrum Sōlī id animal et ōre ac distīnctū pinnārum ā cēterīs avibus dīversum

    the bird is sacred to the Sun, and differs from all the others in its beak and the markings of its feathersTac. Ann. 6.28

  • annum ita dīvīsērunt, ut nōnīs modo diēbus urbānās rēs ūsurpārent, reliquīs septem ut rūra colerent

    they divided the year so that they saw to town business only on every ninth day, and farmed on the other sevenVarr. RR 2 praef. 1

  • atque ita posteā ego bellum et odium nivī indīxī, aliī indūtiās cum eā variē factitābant

    and so from then on I declared war and hatred on snow; others made truces with it now and thenGell. 19.5.10

See also the rest, other, else, everyone.
